- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.4) — model shows reluctance to drop below recent lows.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often delays price declines, especially after strong negative sentiment, leading to overcorrection later.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean before correcting.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Avoid extrapolating upward trends when sentiment turns negative — model often ignores sentiment shift and continues upward momentum.
